title: Daily means removed four joint-exposure contrasts at fixed cutoffs in North Wales domes in August-September 2021
abstract: We tested whether block means preserve joint high-ozone and dry-air exposure counts. We used 1,464 complete hourly records from a North Wales wildflower experiment in August and September 2021. At cutoffs of 2 kPa vapor pressure deficit and 60 ppb ozone, four heated-minus-ambient hourly contrasts were 43 to 92 hours. Daily means gave zero joint exposure at every tested daily start hour with two weather methods. Shorter blocks could understate or overstate the contrast. In one September pair, six-hour contrasts ranged from 66 to 114 hours against an hourly contrast of 92. All 9,936 aggregate rows passed an independent scalar check. The method separates missed and falsely classified hours and uses the same time support for every comparison. These are deterministic record comparisons, not confidence intervals or causal effects. One site-year, one dome per treatment, shared ambient weather, unknown source gap filling and diagnostic cutoffs limit use. No plant injury or biodiversity effect was tested. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, a figure and external retrieval instructions are included. The source records overlap earlier campaign exposure studies; block averaging is the new test.

display.caption: Joint-exposure contrasts from block means at fixed cutoffs and midnight alignment. Daily means give zero at both tested high-ozone targets in both months. These are record summaries, not treatment-effect estimates.

citations.reason: Prior schedule-control study supplies source context. Our raw records overlap; no code is reused.
Prior duration-bound study motivates an observation-method audit. We use its cutoffs and source scope but test block averaging with new code.
